sentences.back: Long ago, the people in the city of ancient Rome needed water.
They lived far from the river.
They made a clever plan to bring water to their homes.
Workers built long stone water channels.
This big project helped bring water from far away.
The water went through deep holes in the hills.
It also went over tall stone bridges.
Water flowed in these channels every day.
Because the ground sloped, the water slowly flowed downhill.
The natural shape of the land pushed the water forward.
This great infrastructure changed daily life.
Clean water came straight to the towns.
People used it for drinking, cooking and washing things.
This clever design kept the city alive and healthy.
